corrections.reason: Pass-1 Reframed is correct. Subsumption test fails ('User-Centric Design is a specific way of being customer-centricity' is not clearly true — UCD is an operational design principle, not a strict subtype of customer orientation), but the pair shares the user/customer-centered semantic neighborhood and the organizing frame shifts from audience-orientation to design-recipient frame. PRE is substantive (customer-centricity), so the sibling reading is appropriate. Confirm Reframed.

After full-response recheck against all five POST concepts, no tier of the ladder is defensible. Quality (attribute/standard) vs User-Centric Design (user-focus), Wellness & Balance (outcome), Innovation & Simplicity (process), Affordability & Accessibility (cost/access), Sustainability (environmental): all are different conceptual domains. Confirmed non-neighborhood; Removed stands.
Nearest PRE (quality) is in a different conceptual domain (attribute standard vs product health-outcome). No transformation tier holds. Confirmed New.

final_alignments.basis: Shared user/customer-centered semantic neighborhood; PRE frames as audience-orientation, POST frames as operational design-recipient principle. Frame shift without subsumption.

semantic_events.post_evidence: User-Centric Design – Focused on real-world needs, ensuring effortless use and convenience.
semantic_events.rationale: Both occupy the user/customer-centered neighborhood. The organizing frame shifts from audience-orientation (centering the customer) to a design-recipient frame (centering the user as the object of design decisions). Subsumption test fails — User-Centric Design is an operational sibling of customer-centricity, not a strict subtype — so tier 2 (Reframed) is the correct verdict. PRE is substantive, reinforcing the sibling reading over a subsumption reading.
semantic_events.alternative_considered: Narrowed (rejected: 'User-Centric Design is a specific way of being customer-centricity' is not literally true; UCD is a design-methodology sibling rather than a customer-orientation subtype)

semantic_events.rationale: After exhaustive recheck against all five POST concepts, quality (as an attribute/standard) sits in a different conceptual domain from each candidate: User-Centric Design (user-focus), Wellness & Balance (product outcome), Innovation & Simplicity (process), Affordability & Accessibility (cost/access), Sustainability (environmental). No tier of the transformation ladder is defensible; no neighborhood is shared.
semantic_events.alternative_considered: Reframed against User-Centric Design (rejected: no shared semantic territory at a specific level — 'attribute standard' and 'user-centered design' are different domains, and the only umbrella would be 'brand value', which hits the abstraction ceiling)

semantic_events.post_evidence: Wellness & Balance – Helping users both fall asleep faster and wake up naturally.
semantic_events.rationale: Nearest PRE concept is quality, which occupies a different conceptual domain (attribute standard vs product health-outcome). Full ladder test fails across all four tiers; no PRE antecedent exists.

semantic_events.post_evidence: Innovation & Simplicity – Using technology in a way that is effective, easy to use, and intuitive.
semantic_events.rationale: Nearest PRE concept is quality, which sits in a different conceptual domain (attribute standard vs innovation/process-design). No transformation tier holds.

semantic_events.post_evidence: Affordability & Accessibility – Making sleep technology accessible to everyone, not just premium users.
semantic_events.rationale: Nearest PRE concept is customer-centricity. Narrowed test fails (accessibility targets non-customers as well, so it is not a subset of customer focus); Reframed/Elaborated/Expanded also fail because cost/access is a different value axis from audience orientation. No PRE antecedent exists.

semantic_events.post_evidence: Sustainability – Using eco-conscious materials and energy-efficient solutions.
semantic_events.rationale: Nearest PRE concept is quality, in a different conceptual domain (attribute standard vs environmental/material sourcing). No transformation tier holds.
